goal: Improve exact-match technical position matching on the public CPU DEV task.
project_context: CPU-only Python matcher; editable production file is solution.py.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Add explicit handling for negation cues and their nearby technical terms in solution.py so statements with opposite polarity do not receive misleadingly similar overlap scores; this will improve exact-match quality by at least 0.001 on the CPU DEV set.
hypothesis.rationale: The task names negation as a possible error class. Token overlap can count shared terms despite a polarity reversal, which a polarity-aware feature could address.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Quality increases by at least 0.001 versus the current champion, with fewer errors on negated statements.
hypothesis.falsification_condition: The DEV quality delta is below 0.001, or polarity handling fails to reduce negation-related errors.
hypothesis.novelty_rationale: Experiments 1–3 reported partial DEV improvements of 0.0002–0.0004, below the required 0.001. Their results support that the tested mechanisms moved quality slightly; they do not test or disprove polarity-aware matching. This proposal changes the matching signal to account for negation.

hypothesis.suspected_failure_mode: Shared content tokens may outweigh a negation cue, making statements with opposite meanings appear similar.
hypothesis.predicted_observable: Negation-related DEV mismatches decrease and overall quality rises by at least 0.001.
hypothesis.discriminating_test: Compare the current champion with a polarity-aware variant on the same DEV set; inspect negation cases and require a total quality delta of at least 0.001.
hypothesis.rationale: Tests whether representing polarity directly resolves a semantic distinction that plain token overlap can obscure.
hypothesis.uncertainty: No supplied DEV breakdown establishes the frequency or impact of negation errors.

task_document.content:
# Technical position matcher

Improve `solution.py`, which matches short technical position statements to
their canonical engineering concepts. The intended metric is exact-match
quality on a fixed CPU-only DEV set. Editable scope is only `solution.py`.
Use the provided public task description and DEV research context to propose a
falsifiable next mechanism. Do not claim measured results that are not present
in the request. The proposer is only asked for hypotheses; this harness does
not implement candidates or run evaluation.

Current implementation uses normalized token overlap. Potential error classes
include synonyms, negation, acronym expansion, and compositional word order.
